content:
Every SOF IMO paper has a dedicated Logical Reasoning section — series, analogies, coding, directions and ranking. It is pure pattern-spotting, and it is trainable. Here is what the Class 6 reasoning section tests, the methods, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 6 Maths Olympiad Logical Reasoning chapter tests

  • Number and letter series
  • Analogies and odd-one-out
  • Coding-decoding (letter shifts and number codes)
  • Directions, ranking and blood relations

Key facts your child should know

  • Write the DIFFERENCES to expose a number rule (+3, ×2, squares…).
  • In a row of N people: left position + right position = N + 1.
  • Right turn = 90° clockwise; track facing and displacement separately.
  • For number codes, match the repeated word across phrases to pin its digit.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Reading letter series without writing alphabet positions.
  • Forgetting the N + 1 rule in ranking questions.
  • Turning the wrong way on "left" after facing south.

questions.q: If A=1, B=2, ..., Z=26, what is the code for CAT?
In a code, 1=A, 2=E, 3=I, 4=O, 5=U. What does 3-1-4 spell?
Ravi walks 5 km North, then 3 km East. How far is he from the starting point?
If sunset is to your right and you face South, sunrise is behind you. True or false?
questions.explanation: Facing South: right = West (sunset), behind = North (not sunrise). Sunrise = East = left. False.

questions.q: In the above diagram, how many like at least one subject?
If all Roses are Flowers, and all Flowers are Beautiful, then what can we conclude?
questions.explanation: If A implies B and B implies C, then A implies C. All Roses are Beautiful.

questions.q: If all cats are animals and some animals are pets, which is definitely true?
questions.explanation: We cannot conclude all cats are pets, only that some may be.

questions.q: In a code, 537 means "sky is blue", 842 means "roses are red", and 358 means "blue are beautiful". What is the code for "are"?
questions.explanation: "are" is the only word common to "roses are red" (842) and "blue are beautiful" (358), and 8 is the only digit those codes share. So "are" = 8.

faq.q: How do I crack number series questions?
faq.a: Write the differences between terms; if they are not constant, check ratios, squares or alternating patterns.
In a row of N, position from left + position from right = N + 1.
